question: Should I replace my account managers with AI or hire a salesperson?
business: Austin performance marketing agency, 18 clients at $3K/mo, 16% margin, $70K cash

hormozi.name: Alex Hormozi
hormozi.question: Does the money math work, and is the offer strong enough to carry it?

musk.question: What is the real constraint, and which step can we delete?

buffett.name: Warren Buffett
buffett.question: What does this do to cash, risk and long-term value?

zuckerberg.question: What will Meta's feed and ads actually reward here?

mrbeast.question: Will people click, and will they keep watching?

1.title: Opening

hormozi.STAKE: in, because lead handling, unit economics and the offer are all in play.
hormozi.THE CALL: Option B, hire the closer on a base-plus-commission deal with a 90-day kill rule, and do not touch the AMs yet.
hormozi.WHY:
1. The leak is in lead handling (H5). I assume 20 to 25 calls a month, and the founder pushes about half of them. A closer who holds those calls at the same 2 in 10 adds about 2 clients a month, or $6,000/mo of new revenue each month.
2. The unit economics clear the bar (H4). A client is worth $3,000/mo, and the closer costs about $3,600 per client in commission, which is 1.2 months of fees. LTV to CAC is well above 3 to 1, assuming a client stays about 12 months.
3. A saves $8,400/mo, but it cuts the people who calm clients when results dip (H6). Churn is already 1 client a month, and 2 of the last 5 leavers cited communication. I'd be paying $23,000 to risk the $3,000/mo clients I already have.
4. The constraint is top-of-funnel conversion, not report cost (H6). Savings don't grow the business. Closed deals do.
hormozi.THE RISK I SEE: The closer closes below 2 in 10, or the founder's pushed calls were low quality. Then I'm out $5,000/mo plus commission for 3 months of ramp, about $15,000, and nothing has changed.
hormozi.WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: Show me that fewer than 5 calls a month are actually pushed or lost, or that the AMs' calming work is under 10 hours a month. Then A's savings win.
hormozi.SAYS:
B. You don't have a report problem, you have a call problem. Half your calls get pushed, and that's about $6,000/mo of MRR leaking.
A saves $8,400 but risks churn on $54,000 of revenue. Fix the leak first, then automate the reports.

musk.STAKE: in. The report work is a step-deletion question, which is my lens.
musk.DOOR: two-way (as a variant; plain A is one-way once the severance is paid)
musk.THE CALL: A variant. Delete the reports with live client dashboards first, then cut one AM, and skip the $14K custom build.
musk.WHY:
1. 60% of two AM weeks is reports and status updates. That is about $5,400/mo of work, and I'd question why it exists before I automate it (M2, M3).
2. Clients asked for more reporting, which means they want to see numbers, not receive emails. A live dashboard deletes the report. The $14K build for 6 weeks is automating before deleting (M4).
3. The limit on growth is the founder's calendar. He pushes half his closes because he is in delivery (M7). Pulling him out of delivery matters more than who writes reports.
4. A dashboard pilot takes days. Test it on 3 clients and keep both AMs until it holds (M6, M8).
musk.THE RISK I SEE: The AMs' other 40% is calming clients when results dip. Remove them and churn goes from 1 a month to 2 or more. That is $3K/mo lost per client, and the cash is only 6 weeks deep.
musk.WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: If the 3-client pilot shows clients still demand emailed reports and calls after the dashboards go live, the step is load-bearing. Then I'd go to C.
musk.SAYS:
I'd delete the reports before I fire anyone. 60% of AM time is a step that shouldn't exist.
$14K and 6 weeks is automating waste. Dashboards on 3 clients take days. Run that first.

buffett.STAKE: in, because it spends 6 weeks of cash on a build and severance.
buffett.THE CALL: Hire the closer on a 90-day trial with the base pay capped, and leave the AMs alone this quarter.
buffett.WHY:
1. Option A spends $23,000 (build plus severance) of a $70,000 cushion. That leaves about 4 weeks of costs in the bank, and the severance can't be undone. I won't trade B4 for a saving I haven't seen yet. (B1, B4)
2. The $8,400/mo saving disappears if AI-run accounts cost you one extra client a month. You already lose one a month, and 2 of the last 5 leavers cited "communication". I'd call that a real chance. (B7)
3. B's worst case is about $15,000 of base pay over the 3-month ramp. Commission is only paid on clients who sign. If he doesn't close, you let him go and keep the AMs. Each client is $3,000/mo, so one close in the ramp starts paying you back. (B3, B7)
4. More clients widens the base. Cutting costs just rents a better margin. I assume the closer matches your 2-in-10 close rate, which is unproven. (B5)
buffett.THE RISK I SEE: The AI build quietly raises churn. If you lose 3 clients, that's $9,000/mo gone, and the cash is already spent.
buffett.WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: Proof from a live pilot on 3 clients showing client retention holds with AI reporting. Or the closer's first 60 days showing under 1 close per 20 calls. Then I'd go with C and keep the cash.
buffett.SAYS:
B, with a 90-day cap. A burns $23k and leaves you 4 weeks of cash. A bad hire costs you $15k at most.
Founder, I get being tired of reports. Pilot the AI on 3 accounts first. Don't fire anyone on a hunch.
